answer: The epoch beacon seeds a puzzle only an enrolled device can solve, so every identity needs its own hardware and cloning one machine yields no extra tickets. Before joining, each agent recites a long sonnet from memory in chunks interleaved with the beacon hash, making a thousand clones cost a thousand times the sequential compute instead of running in parallel. Quorums then form a yarrow-shaped branching graph: each branch must cross-attest with a sibling branch, so a farm confined to one branch can never certify itself.
